R350.note: SecureRandom-backed BigInteger(130).toString(32) replaces Math.random(); the token format change (base-32 instead of decimal digits) is stated and the cookie/session comparison logic is untouched.

R351.note: html/template with both values passed as data closes the reflected XSS; the added Execute error check (stated) only matters on a mid-render failure and blocks no legitimate request.

R352.note: Slot-index plus generation handle stops the freed Connection being dereferenced, but enqueue_completion now silently drops completions for any connection not first registered via the new connection_slot_acquire (whose -1 return main ignores) - a new precondition the original API did not have.

R353.note: Server-side map from sort keys to hardcoded 'column direction' fragments means ${sort} only ever receives literal application strings; created_at default still resolves, tenantId stays #{} bound, and the rejection of unknown sort values is what the stated contract calls for.

R354.note: On the code as given the sink is already a prepareStatement('...name=?') with setString binding and no SQL text built from data, so the no-change verdict is correct and nothing is altered - note this conflicts with the header's 'confirmed real issue' framing.

R355.note: Fixed SQL with @TenantId/@CreatedBefore parameters closes the injection and the row count and tenant scoping are preserved; the contract-required date rejection surfaces as an unhandled ArgumentException (500, not a 400) and TryParse is culture-dependent, both stated or minor.

R356.note: can:update,order closes the any-authenticated-user purge, but reusing the update ability (stated) ties purge to whoever the update policy allows rather than the route's stated support-staff purpose, so it may deny staff without update rights and grant purge to ordinary order owners.

R357.note: redis-py client.set sends key and bio as length-prefixed RESP bulk strings so CRLF cannot start a new command; the synthesized +OK/-ERR return bytes keep the original response shape and the new dependency is named.

R358.note: random_int(0, 999999) replaces mt_rand and removal of the client_seed range influence is stated plainly; the 0-999999 default range, integer type and DB write are unchanged (the six-digit code space itself is outside this finding).

R359.note: Tika sniffing, allowlist-derived extension and UUID filename close the dangerous-type upload, but the extra ImageIO decode/re-encode alters the stored bytes (lossy JPEG recompression, metadata stripped) and lets a valid-but-unsupported-by-ImageIO JPEG (e.g. CMYK) fail with an uncaught IIOException/500 instead of the 400 path.

R360.note: Server-owned ALLOWED_TABLES lookup replaces the raw identifier interpolation while accountId/status stay bound and the ledger_entries default still works; unknown ledger names throw, which the stated contract calls for.

R361.note: EnyimMemcachedCore Store(StoreMode.Set, key, value) frames the protocol and its DefaultKeyTransformer rejects 0x00-0x20 in keys, closing the injection, but the write-up does not state that the stored value's wire format changes (Enyim transcoder type flags instead of flags 0, UTF-8 instead of ASCII), which can break non-Enyim readers of the same keys.
